# 1.1.0
Bump: minor

- Reduce optimized executable size with fat LTO and one codegen unit, retaining optimization level 3, existing CLI features and runtime requirements. Release builds require more optimization/link work.

- Execute an HTTPS/SSH revision outside a checkout or select a configured remote: `git on origin main -- command args`. One operand still selects a local revision; two select repository and revision. Put keep and verification options after REV; the command tail remains literal after `--`.
- Fetch exact objects on demand with a persistent cache bounded to 256 MiB and 4096 objects. Concurrent eviction preserves active run copies. Active temporary objects and ignored writes have no runner quota. No full checkout or full-clone fallback is introduced.
- Reuse an authenticated OpenSSH connection for lazy fetches. An unlocked agent needs no passphrase prompt; one selected encrypted identity authenticates before mounting. Lost connections and filter/OID rejection fail with precise diagnostics.
- Keep SSH argument boundaries structural, so expanding the owned control path in caller options cannot leave master flags active or reconnect after connection loss.
- Report failed `.gitignore` object/cache acquisition as `EIO` for file and directory creation, retain `EINTR` for interrupted requests, and keep ordinary write-policy denials as `EROFS`.
- Relay Ctrl-Z and `fg`/`bg` between git-on and native Git during SSH authentication, restoring foreground terminal ownership and preserving interrupt cleanup.
- Add `--verify` with native Git `verify-commit`/`verify-tag` on the exact resolved object and effective configuration, including inherited `git -c`. Git owns formats and trust; git-on adds no signer allowlist or trust threshold. Git's default may accept unknown-trust OpenPGP, while a configured `gpg.minTrustLevel` can reject it before mounting or execution. Signed tags and directory selectors remain bound to exact objects. Disable replacements consistently.
- Preserve Git-free direct local execution without `--verify`. Explicit remote HEAD/full refs remain literal selections even when colliding short names or unrelated non-UTF-8 refs are advertised; help displays runner options after REV.
- Generate structured help and contextual usage errors with clap. Keep command argv literal after the required `--`, existing argument compatibility, cleanup behavior and exit statuses. Use `git on -h` to display help through Git.
- Reject peeled tag advertisement helpers as remote refs; preserve the exact selected verification object. Handle termination signals before the first native Git operation, and close persistent SSH connections with the selected client outside `PATH`. Failed owned shutdown preserves recovery state. SIGKILL leaves disconnected mounts and can leave command/transport processes; stop their users externally before checked cleanup.

Remote execution requires Git 2.45.1+, a filtering server allowing requested OIDs and existing credentials. Remote ancestry/reflog/abbreviated-ID syntax, non-OpenSSH variants and SSH command shell prefixes/compounds are unsupported. Transparent `GIT_SSH` executables forwarding OpenSSH arguments are supported. Multiple encrypted identities or separately authenticated jump hosts may require extra initial interaction. See `docs/remote.md` for limits. Local syntax and filesystem policy remain compatible with 1.0.0. Verification does not certify tests or provide sandbox safety.
